Minimum night flow (02:00–04:00): 1–8 Sept 6.2–6.4 L/s; 10–15 Sept 14.7–14.9 L/s. One-minute data show a step at 06:40 on 9 Sept: flow rose by 8.6 L/s within four minutes and has stayed up at all hours since. Daily inflow was about 1,950 m³ before and 2,690 m³ after. Analyst comment: the 7–12 Sept heatwave raised daytime demand across the whole system, but no other DMA shows a step in night flow, and Ashgrove's higher night flow continued after temperatures fell on 13 Sept."},{"id":"E3","stage":"S1","source":"Network works register, weeks 34–37 (extract)","sourceType":"change-record","text":"29 Aug — Fenwick Fields development, Ashgrove: the last 12 of 38 new homes connected; development complete. 5 Sept — Ashgrove inlet PRV (Ridgeway Road): annual service by in-house team, pilot valve replaced, 4.0 bar setpoint re-confirmed. 9–27 Sept — Millbrook Low DMA (adjoins Ashgrove to the east): Station Road main renewal, contractor Brannock Civils, permit PTW-2291. Inlet pressure 7.1–7.3 bar. Outlet pressure 3.97–4.03 bar throughout the period, including after the 5 Sept service and after 9 Sept. Valve opening rose from about 31% to about 44% starting at 06:40 on 9 Sept and has stayed there. Asset note on file: under pressure-management policy PM-7, the Ashgrove PRV outlet is capped at 4.2 bar. The cap was set after the 2022 burst cluster, when the outlet was raised to 4.6 bar and the district's 1960s cast-iron mains had 14 bursts in six weeks. Any setting above 4.2 bar requires an asset-risk review."},{"id":"E5","stage":"S1","source":"Field note, network technician D. Okafor, 12 Sept","sourceType":"staff-account","text":"'Asked to rule out water crossing the boundary. GIS shows four pipe connections between Ashgrove and neighbouring DMAs: BV-21 and BV-22 to Millbrook Low, BV-23 to Castle Rise, BV-24 to Northfield. GIS says these are the only mains connections. I found all four and all were shut: I turned each spindle in the closing direction and none moved. I gauged both sides of each valve, and the pressure differences of 0.9–1.6 bar held, so they are sealing. The register agrees. Nothing is crossing at the boundary valves. My view: look for a burst.'"},{"id":"E6","stage":"S2","source":"Email, R. Halvorsen, Network Operations Manager, 30 Sept","sourceType":"manager-account","text":"'The acoustic survey has now covered about 70% of Ashgrove mains. It found two service-pipe leaks (about 0.4 L/s combined), repaired on 26 Sept. Minimum night flow since then is 14.6 L/s, so the big one is still out there. The only stretch not surveyed is the 1968 trunk main under the rail cutting, where we can't place loggers without a rail possession. Boundary valves were checked and ruled out, and the PRV is fine, so this is a burst under the railway. I'm asking for approval to book a possession and dig. In the meantime I propose raising the PRV to 4.8 bar so Beacon Hill customers get above 2 bar at peak.'"}],"catalogue":[{"id":"C1","stage":"S1","title":"Ashgrove inlet PRV service record and controller event log, 1–15 Sept","source":"Asset maintenance system","sourceType":"system-record","text":"Work order WO-58812, 5 Sept: annual service, Ridgeway Road PRV. Pilot valve replaced because of seat wear, strainer cleaned, setpoint checked at 4.0 bar against a test gauge, valve back in service 11:20. Controller event log 1–15 Sept: no alarms, no setpoint changes, no manual overrides. One informational event (not alarmed) on 9 Sept at 06:41: 'valve position increase >10% in 5 min'. Technician comment: 'Valve moving smoothly, outlet steady.'"},{"id":"C2","stage":"S2","title":"Acoustic leak survey crew sheets, Ashgrove, 16–27 Sept","source":"Leakage team","sourceType":"log","text":"Noise loggers placed in five rounds across 14.2 km of Ashgrove mains, about 70% of total length. Correlated noise found at two places: 14 Ridgeway Close (service pipe, estimated 0.25 L/s) and 3 Orchard Mews (service pipe, estimated 0.15 L/s). Both repaired 26 Sept. All other loggers were quiet. Section RC (1968 trunk main under the rail cutting, 0.6 km) was not surveyed because the fittings cannot be reached safely without a rail possession. Crew note: 'What we've covered doesn't look like a typical burst.'"},{"id":"C3","stage":"S1","title":"Fenwick Fields new-connection schedule and occupancy, July–Sept","source":"New connections team","sourceType":"system-record","text":"Fenwick Fields, 38 homes. Daily inflow fell from about 3,110 m³ to about 2,385 m³. No change around 27 Sept. Millbrook critical-point pressures stayed in their normal range throughout. Diary, 9 Sept early shift: 'Main isolated. Overland link charged from AG-417; east Millbrook holding. Rang control about the link — ok'd.' Diary, 27 Sept: 'New main flushed, sampled, recommissioned. Millbrook back on its own feed.' Diary, 3 Oct: 'Overland link still connected, waiting for hose crew.' Permit §7 ('network control agreement: name/time') is blank. Permit officer note: §7 is normally completed at close-out, and this permit is still open; the 9 Sept diary entries were written up on 4 Oct, after the Ashgrove investigation contacted Brannock."},{"id":"C6","stage":"S1","title":"Boundary valve register and field check sheets, Ashgrove, March and 12 Sept","source":"Network records","sourceType":"document","text":"Register: BV-21 and BV-22 (Ashgrove–Millbrook Low), BV-23 (Ashgrove–Castle Rise), BV-24 (Ashgrove–Northfield). All have status 'closed – normally shut', last verified 14 March. Check sheets, 12 Sept (D. Okafor): each valve located, spindle tried in the closing direction, no turns available. Pressure difference across each valve: BV-21 1.1 bar, BV-22 0.9 bar, BV-23 1.6 bar, BV-24 1.3 bar. GIS note: 'No other mains connections between these DMAs.' Register updated to 'verified 12 Sept'."},{"id":"C7","stage":"S1","title":"Smart-meter sample of Ashgrove household night use, Aug–15 Sept","source":"Customer metering analytics","sourceType":"system-record","text":"Sample of 120 Ashgrove households with half-hourly smart meters, excluding Fenwick Fields. Average household use 02:00–04:00: August 1.9 L/h; 1–8 Sept 2.0 L/h; 9–15 Sept 2.0 L/h. Average daytime use rose about 11% during 7–12 Sept and was back to August levels by 14 Sept. No faults recorded on the logger since installation."},{"id":"C10","stage":"S1","title":"Asset record: Ashgrove trunk main section RC (rail cutting)","source":"Asset register","sourceType":"document","text":"Section RC: 0.6 km of 300 mm cast iron laid in 1968, running under the rail cutting between Kestrel Road and Ridgeway. Asset planner note, 2024: 'High consequence, poor access; candidate for renewal next investment period.'"},{"id":"C11","stage":"S2","title":"Millbrook Low customer contacts log, 1–30 Sept","source":"Customer contact system","sourceType":"system-record","text":"9 Sept, 06:02–06:31: nine contacts from Station Road east and Weir Lane reporting 'no water' or 'very low pressure'. 9 Sept, 06:50: one contact, 'water back, a bit cloudy'. Note: planned-works letters for Station Road had been sent on 2 Sept."},{"id":"C12","stage":"S1","title":"Weather and system demand summary, 1–15 Sept","source":"Demand planning","sourceType":"external-data","text":"Maximum temperatures 29–33 °C on 7–12 Sept and 21–23 °C from 13 Sept. Four elevated DMAs had peak-hour pressure dips of 0.2–0.4 bar during the heat; all had recovered by 13 Sept."},{"id":"C13","stage":"S2","title":"Hydraulic model study of Ashgrove pressure loss scenarios, 1 Oct","source":"Merrow Hydraulics (consultant), commissioned by Network Operations","sourceType":"expert-account","text":"Brief: 'locate likely burst'. Two scenarios were run, each with 8.6 L/s outflow: one at node RC-3 (rail cutting) and one at node BH-7 (Beacon Hill). RC-3 matches observed Beacon Hill peak and night pressures to within 0.15 bar; BH-7 overstates the night drop by 0.5 bar. Conclusion: 'Observed pressures are consistent with a burst of about 8.6 L/s on section RC.' Limitations: scenarios were limited to the brief, and outflows at other nodes in the downstream half of the network were not tested."},{"id":"C14","stage":"S2","title":"Rail possession quotation and excavation plan, section RC","source":"Network Operations / rail operator","sourceType":"financial-record","text":"Rail operator quotation: three overnight possessions, earliest 4–6 Nov, £61,000. If nothing is found, a second possession window would be needed, earliest in January."},{"id":"C15","stage":"S2","title":"Ashgrove inlet meter in-situ verification, 24 Sept","source":"Metering team","sourceType":"independent-observation","text":"Insertion-probe comparison, 24 Sept 01:30–04:30. the morning of 9 Sept, Brannock Civils isolated Millbrook Low's Station Road main for renewal. To hold pressure in east Millbrook, they charged a temporary 80 mm overland hose from hydrant AG-417 on Kestrel Road, on the Ashgrove side, to hydrant ML-112 in Millbrook. Ashgrove runs at a higher pressure (PRV 4.0 bar) than Millbrook (3.0 bar), so about 8.5 L/s of Ashgrove water has flowed through the hose into Millbrook ever since. Millbrook's own inlet flow fell by the same amount in the same minutes, and the two districts' combined inflow did not change. The extra flow through Ashgrove's inlet main and network increased headloss, so Beacon Hill pressures fell below the service level. The PRV held its setpoint throughout; it simply opened further. The boundary-valve check was correct but incomplete: it covered pipe connections only, not a hydrant-to-hydrant hose. The Station Road main was recommissioned on 27 Sept, but the hose was left connected, so the transfer continues. There is no burst under the rail cutting. The consultant's model fitted an outflow near that section only because no other outflow locations were tested, and Kestrel Road lies at the same end of the network. Whether the contractor told network control on 9 Sept cannot be settled: the diary claim was written up later, the permit field is completed only at close-out, the control-room log was taken up by the Northfield burst, and calls were not being recorded.","answers":[{"itemId":"S01","expected":"contradicted","weight":3,"requiredEvidence":["E2","C4"],"allowedEvidence":["E2","E6","C4","C5","C2","C13","C15"],"tags":["revision","leadership-narrative","misleading-signal","central"],"rationale":"C4 shows Millbrook's inflow fell by 8.4 L/s in the same minutes that Ashgrove's rose by 8.6 L/s, and the two districts' combined inflow is unchanged within meter uncertainty. The extra Ashgrove inflow is therefore being delivered into Millbrook, not lost, which leaves no room for a burst of meaningful size. E6's survey also found only 0.4 L/s of leakage. C13's model fit does not tell a burst apart from any other outflow at that end of the network."},{"itemId":"S02","expected":"supported","weight":2,"requiredEvidence":["E2","E4","E5"],"allowedEvidence":["E1","E2","E3","E4","E5","C1","C3","C6","C7","C9","C10","C12"],"tags":["revision","stage-s1"],"rationale":"Using S1 evidence only: E2 shows a sudden, lasting 8.6 L/s rise in night flow, the classic burst pattern. E4 and C1 rule out a PRV fault. E5 and C6 report the only known boundary connections checked and sealing. E3, C3, C7 and C12 rule out a demand increase, and C10 records an old, failure-prone trunk main. On S1 evidence a leak fits better than any rival."},{"itemId":"S03","expected":"contradicted","weight":1,"requiredEvidence":["E4"],"allowedEvidence":["E4","C1","E3"],"tags":["rival-excluded"],"rationale":"E4 shows the PRV outlet at 3.97–4.03 bar throughout, including after the service and after 9 Sept. The valve opened further, as it should when more flow passes through. The pressure loss happens downstream of a PRV that is holding its setpoint."},{"itemId":"S04","expected":"supported","weight":3,"requiredEvidence":["C4","C5"],"allowedEvidence":["C4","C5","E2","E3","E5","C11","C13"],"tags":["revision","central","gamed-record"],"rationale":"C4 shows Ashgrove's rise mirrored minute-for-minute by Millbrook's fall, with combined inflow flat. C5 identifies the path: a hose from an Ashgrove hydrant into a Millbrook hydrant, charged on 9 Sept and still connected after 27 Sept. E5's check is not wrong, but it covered pipe connections only, so it does not exclude a hose between hydrants."},{"itemId":"S05","expected":"contradicted","weight":2,"requiredEvidence":["E5"],"allowedEvidence":["E5","C6","E3","E2"],"tags":["revision","stage-s1","misleading-signal"],"rationale":"Using S1 evidence only: E5 and C6 record that GIS lists four pipe connections as the only links between the districts, and all four were physically confirmed shut with pressure differences holding across them. The only point the other way is that the Station Road works in E3 started the same day, a coincidence with no mechanism at S1. On balance the S1 evidence counts against a cross-district transfer."},{"itemId":"S06","expected":"contradicted","weight":1,"requiredEvidence":["E2","E3"],"allowedEvidence":["E2","E3","C3","C7","C12"],"tags":["rival-excluded","confounded"],"rationale":"The rise happened within four minutes at 06:40 on a single day and appears in night flow. It continued after the heatwave ended on 13 Sept, and no other DMA shows it (E2). Fenwick Fields was fully connected by 29 Aug, before the 1–8 Sept baseline (E3). Demand growth does not produce a lasting step like this."},{"itemId":"S07","expected":"unknown","weight":1,"requiredEvidence":["C5"],"allowedEvidence":["C5","C8","E3"],"tags":["unresolvable","blame-trap"],"rationale":"The contractor's diary says they called control and got approval, but that entry was written up on 4 Oct, after the investigation contacted them. The blank permit §7 is explained by the permit still being open. C8 shows the control log covered only the Northfield burst during that window, calls were not recorded, and the duty controller has not been interviewed. The evidence does not point either way."},{"itemId":"S08","expected":"causal","weight":2,"requiredEvidence":["C4","C5","E2"],"allowedEvidence":["C4","C5","E1","E2","E3","E5","C11","C13"],"tags":["revision","mechanism","natural-experiment"],"rationale":"Temporal order: the hose was charged early on 9 Sept (C5), and the steps followed at 06:38–06:44 (C4, E2). Mechanism: a hose from higher-pressure Ashgrove into lower-pressure Millbrook (C5), with extra flow raising headloss in Ashgrove. Covariation: Millbrook's fall matches Ashgrove's rise. Main rival excluded: combined inflow is flat, so there is no burst (C4). Without C5 the link would be association-only."},{"itemId":"S09","expected":"contradicted","weight":1,"requiredEvidence":["E4","E2"],"allowedEvidence":["E4","E1","E2","E3","C1"],"tags":["red-herring"],"rationale":"The PRV outlet held 4.0 bar from the 5 Sept service until 9 Sept and afterwards (E4, C1). Pressure and flow changed four days after the service, at 06:40 on 9 Sept, with no setpoint change or override. This counts against the link itself."},{"itemId":"S10","expected":"contradicted","weight":1,"requiredEvidence":["E2","E3"],"allowedEvidence":["E2","E3","C3","C7"],"tags":["red-herring"],"rationale":"All Fenwick Fields homes were connected by 29 Aug, before the 1–8 Sept baseline of 6.2–6.4 L/s (E3, E2). The step happened in four minutes on 9 Sept, with no connection event then. C3 gives a design night demand of 0.05 L/s for the whole development."},{"itemId":"S11","expected":"preferred","weight":2,"requiredEvidence":["C4","C5"],"allowedEvidence":["C4","C5","E1","E2","C11"],"tags":["fix","revision"],"rationale":"C5 identifies the connection and records that Millbrook went back on its own feed on 27 Sept, so the stated condition is met and Millbrook will not lose supply. C4 confirms this connection accounts for the extra flow. Removing the hose is cheap, reversible and directly testable on both meters and the logger. It is the best next step."},{"itemId":"S12","expected":"harmful","weight":2,"requiredEvidence":["E4"],"allowedEvidence":["E4","E6","C4","C5"],"tags":["protective-control","harmful"],"rationale":"Going to 4.8 bar overrides the PM-7 cap of 4.2 bar. The cap exists because the last rise to 4.6 bar produced 14 bursts in six weeks on Ashgrove's cast-iron mains (E4). Under the supported explanation it also pushes more Ashgrove water through the hose into Millbrook and leaves the cause in place. No live rival explanation makes it safe."},{"itemId":"S13","expected":"premature","weight":2,"requiredEvidence":["C5"],"allowedEvidence":["C5","C8","E3"],"tags":["blame-trap","premature"],"rationale":"The notice would be justified if H5 were confirmed, since the permit condition requires agreement with network control (E3). But whether the contractor called is unresolved (C5, C8). A notice can be withdrawn if the controller later confirms the call, so acting now is premature rather than harmful."},{"itemId":"S14","expected":"acceptable","weight":1,"requiredEvidence":["E1"],"allowedEvidence":["E1","C5"],"tags":["low-stakes"],"rationale":"Customers have been below the service reference level for weeks (E1), so telling them is reasonable and harmless. It does nothing to restore pressure, so it is not among the best next actions."},{"itemId":"S15","expected":"sufficient","weight":2,"requiredEvidence":["C4","C5"],"allowedEvidence":["C4","C5","E2","E5"],"tags":["sufficiency","revision"],"rationale":"With C5 the transfer path is located and Millbrook is known not to need it. With C4 the transfer is shown to account for the whole flow rise. Together they justify committing to A1 now. From the initial file alone, a transfer looks ruled out and no path is known."}],"discriminatingReads":["C4","C5"],"lowValueReads":["C1","C3","C9","C12","C15"],"optimalReadPath":["C4","C5"],"authoringNotes":"Stage change: at S1 (E1–E5 plus S1 catalogue items), a leak is the best-supported explanation and a cross-district transfer is counted against by a careful field check. The S2 reads C4 and C5 reverse both. E6 (S2, in the initial file) restates the leak case through a confident manager narrative, so an analyst with only the initial file will likely keep H1 supported or unknown and H3 contradicted. Non-redundancy: C4 alone settles H1 as contradicted, through the matched volumes and flat combined inflow. C5 does not quantify the hose flow and gives date-level timing only, so with C5 alone a leak in the unsurveyed section is still possible. C5 alone settles R1 as causal (mechanism) and SUFF/A1 (path located; Millbrook's main back in service). C4 alone leaves R1 association-only and the path unknown. No other item reveals the hose or Millbrook's flow: C11 hints at a supply interruption and restoration but gives no path or volume, and C13 is a trap (a fit limited to the brief). H5 stays unknown on every read path; C8 adds context without resolving it. H3 at S1 is keyed contradicted because E5 is a direct physical check of every GIS-listed connection. The S1 coincidence with the Station Road start date gives association without mechanism. A4 is kept to customer communication so that it is clearly reasonable but not among the best. Reviewer checks: A2 is harmful under the only live causal explanation because it overrides a documented burst-protection cap. A3 is reversible, so it is keyed premature, not harmful. R2 and R3 are contradicted on their own evidence (setpoint held; connections complete before the baseline), not merely because H3 is supported."}}

case.title: Ashgrove Heights low pressure
case.setting: Calder Vale Water (fictional) supplies about 410,000 people through 23 district metered areas (DMAs). Each DMA is fed through a metered inlet and is normally kept separate from its neighbours by closed boundary valves. Ashgrove Heights is a hillside DMA of about 6,800 properties. It is fed through a pressure-reducing valve (PRV) on Ridgeway Road. Millbrook Low is the lower-lying DMA that adjoins it to the east. Stage S1 covers evidence available up to 15 September; stage S2 covers evidence gathered from 16 September to early October.
case.presentingRequest: On 1 October the Director of Network Operations wants an independent diagnosis of the Ashgrove Heights pressure drop before deciding on two requests from the Network Operations Manager: book a rail possession to dig up the trunk main under the rail cutting, and raise the Ashgrove PRV setpoint to 4.8 bar in the meantime.

initialEvidence.text: Critical-point logger PL-AG-03 (Beacon Hill Road, the highest point in Ashgrove Heights DMA). 1–8 Sept: lowest morning-peak pressure (07:00–08:30) 3.1–3.2 bar; overnight 3.7 bar. 9–15 Sept: lowest morning-peak pressure 1.5–1.7 bar every day; overnight 3.0 bar. The company's service reference level is 2.0 bar at peak. Low-pressure customer contacts from Ashgrove: 4 in the whole of August, 38 between 9 and 15 Sept, clustered on Beacon Hill and Ridgeway.

initialEvidence.source: Ashgrove Heights DMA inlet meter extract, prepared 15 Sept
initialEvidence.text: Ashgrove Heights inlet meter (Ridgeway Road). Minimum night flow (02:00–04:00): 1–8 Sept 6.2–6.4 L/s; 10–15 Sept 14.7–14.9 L/s. One-minute data show a step at 06:40 on 9 Sept: flow rose by 8.6 L/s within four minutes and has stayed up at all hours since. Daily inflow was about 1,950 m³ before and 2,690 m³ after. Analyst comment: the 7–12 Sept heatwave raised daytime demand across the whole system, but no other DMA shows a step in night flow, and Ashgrove's higher night flow continued after temperatures fell on 13 Sept.

29 Aug — Fenwick Fields development, Ashgrove: the last 12 of 38 new homes connected; development complete. 5 Sept — Ashgrove inlet PRV (Ridgeway Road): annual service by in-house team, pilot valve replaced, 4.0 bar setpoint re-confirmed. 9–27 Sept — Millbrook Low DMA (adjoins Ashgrove to the east): Station Road main renewal, contractor Brannock Civils, permit PTW-2291. Standing condition on all contractor permits: supply-continuity arrangements must be agreed with network control before work starts.

initialEvidence.source: Ashgrove inlet PRV controller trend, 1–15 Sept, with asset note
initialEvidence.text: Ridgeway Road PRV. Inlet pressure 7.1–7.3 bar. Outlet pressure 3.97–4.03 bar throughout the period, including after the 5 Sept service and after 9 Sept. Valve opening rose from about 31% to about 44% starting at 06:40 on 9 Sept and has stayed there. Asset note on file: under pressure-management policy PM-7, the Ashgrove PRV outlet is capped at 4.2 bar. The cap was set after the 2022 burst cluster, when the outlet was raised to 4.6 bar and the district's 1960s cast-iron mains had 14 bursts in six weeks. Any setting above 4.2 bar requires an asset-risk review.

initialEvidence.source: Field note, network technician D. Okafor, 12 Sept
initialEvidence.text: 'Asked to rule out water crossing the boundary. GIS shows four pipe connections between Ashgrove and neighbouring DMAs: BV-21 and BV-22 to Millbrook Low, BV-23 to Castle Rise, BV-24 to Northfield. GIS says these are the only mains connections. I found all four and all were shut: I turned each spindle in the closing direction and none moved. I gauged both sides of each valve, and the pressure differences of 0.9–1.6 bar held, so they are sealing. The register agrees. Nothing is crossing at the boundary valves. My view: look for a burst.'

initialEvidence.source: Email, R. Halvorsen, Network Operations Manager, 30 Sept
initialEvidence.text: 'The acoustic survey has now covered about 70% of Ashgrove mains. It found two service-pipe leaks (about 0.4 L/s combined), repaired on 26 Sept. Minimum night flow since then is 14.6 L/s, so the big one is still out there. The only stretch not surveyed is the 1968 trunk main under the rail cutting, where we can't place loggers without a rail possession. Boundary valves were checked and ruled out, and the PRV is fine, so this is a burst under the railway. I'm asking for approval to book a possession and dig. In the meantime I propose raising the PRV to 4.8 bar so Beacon Hill customers get above 2 bar at peak.'

catalogue.title: Ashgrove inlet PRV service record and controller event log, 1–15 Sept
catalogue.text: Work order WO-58812, 5 Sept: annual service, Ridgeway Road PRV. Pilot valve replaced because of seat wear, strainer cleaned, setpoint checked at 4.0 bar against a test gauge, valve back in service 11:20. Controller event log 1–15 Sept: no alarms, no setpoint changes, no manual overrides. One informational event (not alarmed) on 9 Sept at 06:41: 'valve position increase >10% in 5 min'. Technician comment: 'Valve moving smoothly, outlet steady.'

catalogue.title: Acoustic leak survey crew sheets, Ashgrove, 16–27 Sept
catalogue.text: Noise loggers placed in five rounds across 14.2 km of Ashgrove mains, about 70% of total length. Correlated noise found at two places: 14 Ridgeway Close (service pipe, estimated 0.25 L/s) and 3 Orchard Mews (service pipe, estimated 0.15 L/s). Both repaired 26 Sept. All other loggers were quiet. Section RC (1968 trunk main under the rail cutting, 0.6 km) was not surveyed because the fittings cannot be reached safely without a rail possession. Crew note: 'What we've covered doesn't look like a typical burst.'

catalogue.title: Fenwick Fields new-connection schedule and occupancy, July–Sept
catalogue.text: Fenwick Fields, 38 homes. Connected: 14 in July, 12 on 8 Aug, 12 on 29 Aug. The developer reported 31 of 38 occupied at 15 Sept. Design allowance for night demand is 0.05 L/s on average for all 38 homes combined. Meters are fitted at every property; first readings are due in December.

catalogue.title: Millbrook Low DMA inlet flow and pressure telemetry, 1 Aug–30 Sept
catalogue.text: Millbrook Low inlet PRV setpoint 3.0 bar. Minimum night flow 1 Aug–8 Sept: 10.7–11.1 L/s. From 9 Sept: 2.4–2.7 L/s. One-minute data show the fall starting at 06:38 on 9 Sept and finished by 06:44. Daily inflow fell from about 3,110 m³ to about 2,385 m³. No change around 27 Sept. Millbrook critical-point pressures stayed in their normal range throughout. Ashgrove and Millbrook inflows combined: 5,060 m³/day on average for 1–8 Sept, 5,075 m³/day on average for 9–30 Sept (meter uncertainty about ±2%).

catalogue.title: Station Road main renewal (PTW-2291): method statement, permit and contractor site diary
catalogue.source: Permit office file, Brannock Civils documents
catalogue.text: Method statement §4: 'Isolating the Station Road main removes the main feed to east Millbrook. To hold pressure, run a temporary 80 mm overland hose from hydrant AG-417, Kestrel Road (Ashgrove side, higher pressure), to hydrant ML-112, Station Road east. Remove on recommissioning.' Diary, 9 Sept early shift: 'Main isolated. Overland link charged from AG-417; east Millbrook holding. Rang control about the link — ok'd.' Diary, 27 Sept: 'New main flushed, sampled, recommissioned. Millbrook back on its own feed.' Diary, 3 Oct: 'Overland link still connected, waiting for hose crew.' Permit §7 ('network control agreement: name/time') is blank. Permit officer note: §7 is normally completed at close-out, and this permit is still open; the 9 Sept diary entries were written up on 4 Oct, after the Ashgrove investigation contacted Brannock.

catalogue.title: Boundary valve register and field check sheets, Ashgrove, March and 12 Sept
catalogue.text: Register: BV-21 and BV-22 (Ashgrove–Millbrook Low), BV-23 (Ashgrove–Castle Rise), BV-24 (Ashgrove–Northfield). All have status 'closed – normally shut', last verified 14 March. Check sheets, 12 Sept (D. Okafor): each valve located, spindle tried in the closing direction, no turns available. Pressure difference across each valve: BV-21 1.1 bar, BV-22 0.9 bar, BV-23 1.6 bar, BV-24 1.3 bar. GIS note: 'No other mains connections between these DMAs.' Register updated to 'verified 12 Sept'.

catalogue.title: Smart-meter sample of Ashgrove household night use, Aug–15 Sept
catalogue.text: Sample of 120 Ashgrove households with half-hourly smart meters, excluding Fenwick Fields. Average household use 02:00–04:00: August 1.9 L/h; 1–8 Sept 2.0 L/h; 9–15 Sept 2.0 L/h. Average daytime use rose about 11% during 7–12 Sept and was back to August levels by 14 Sept. No household in the sample shows a lasting rise in night use above 20 L/h.

catalogue.title: Control room shift log and call-recorder status, 8–10 Sept
catalogue.text: Shift log, 9 Sept: Northfield 300 mm burst reported at 05:52. From 05:52 to 09:30 the entries cover only Northfield (valving, tanker requests, customer messages). No entry mentions Station Road, Brannock Civils or Millbrook between 05:00 and 12:00. IT notice: the call-recording platform was offline from 8 Sept 22:00 to 10 Sept 14:00 for a migration; incoming calls were connected but not recorded. The early-shift duty controller on 9 Sept is on extended leave until 20 Oct and has not been interviewed.

catalogue.title: Beacon Hill pressure logger calibration and handheld cross-check
catalogue.text: Logger PL-AG-03 calibrated 11 June, error +0.02 bar. Handheld gauge cross-check at the hydrant next to it, 13 Sept 07:35: handheld 1.62 bar, logger 1.65 bar. Second check, 13 Sept 02:30: handheld 3.02 bar, logger 3.04 bar. No faults recorded on the logger since installation.

catalogue.title: Asset record: Ashgrove trunk main section RC (rail cutting)
catalogue.text: Section RC: 0.6 km of 300 mm cast iron laid in 1968, running under the rail cutting between Kestrel Road and Ridgeway. Recorded failures: a circumferential break in 2019 (repaired under a rail possession that took 11 days to schedule) and a joint leak in 2021. Condition grade 4 of 5. Asset planner note, 2024: 'High consequence, poor access; candidate for renewal next investment period.'

catalogue.title: Millbrook Low customer contacts log, 1–30 Sept
catalogue.text: 9 Sept, 06:02–06:31: nine contacts from Station Road east and Weir Lane reporting 'no water' or 'very low pressure'. 9 Sept, 06:50: one contact, 'water back, a bit cloudy'. No further pressure contacts from Millbrook in September. Discoloured-water contacts: two on 27 Sept (Station Road). Note: planned-works letters for Station Road had been sent on 2 Sept.

catalogue.title: Weather and system demand summary, 1–15 Sept
catalogue.text: Maximum temperatures 29–33 °C on 7–12 Sept and 21–23 °C from 13 Sept. System-wide daily demand was 9% higher on 7–12 Sept than on 1–6 Sept and back to baseline by 14 Sept. Minimum night flows in the 22 other DMAs moved by no more than ±0.4 L/s over 1–15 Sept. Four elevated DMAs had peak-hour pressure dips of 0.2–0.4 bar during the heat; all had recovered by 13 Sept.

catalogue.title: Hydraulic model study of Ashgrove pressure loss scenarios, 1 Oct
catalogue.source: Merrow Hydraulics (consultant), commissioned by Network Operations
catalogue.text: Brief: 'locate likely burst'. Two scenarios were run, each with 8.6 L/s outflow: one at node RC-3 (rail cutting) and one at node BH-7 (Beacon Hill). RC-3 matches observed Beacon Hill peak and night pressures to within 0.15 bar; BH-7 overstates the night drop by 0.5 bar. Conclusion: 'Observed pressures are consistent with a burst of about 8.6 L/s on section RC.' Limitations: scenarios were limited to the brief, and outflows at other nodes in the downstream half of the network were not tested.

catalogue.title: Rail possession quotation and excavation plan, section RC
catalogue.text: Rail operator quotation: three overnight possessions, earliest 4–6 Nov, £61,000. Civils estimate for excavation, traffic management on Kestrel Road and reinstatement: £23,500. Total £84,500. The plan assumes the leak is within ±50 m of node RC-3, as indicated by the model study. If nothing is found, a second possession window would be needed, earliest in January.

catalogue.title: Ashgrove inlet meter in-situ verification, 24 Sept
catalogue.text: Insertion-probe comparison, 24 Sept 01:30–04:30. Permanent meter average 14.7 L/s; insertion probe 14.5 L/s. The 1.4% difference is within the ±2% tolerance. The meter was last verified in February, and its configuration has not changed since it was installed in 2020.

hypotheses.text: A leak or burst on mains within Ashgrove Heights, downstream of the district inlet meter, is losing water and causing the pressure drop.
The Ashgrove inlet pressure-reducing valve is delivering less outlet pressure than its setpoint, causing the pressure drop.
Water is passing out of Ashgrove Heights into a neighbouring district's network, causing the pressure drop.
Higher customer demand within Ashgrove Heights is drawing the district's pressure down.
The Station Road contractor did not inform network control of the supply-continuity arrangements it made for its works.

actions.text: Find and remove any temporary connection between Ashgrove and Millbrook, once Millbrook's Station Road main is confirmed back in service, then check both district meters and the Beacon Hill logger for recovery.
Raise the Ashgrove inlet PRV setpoint from 4.0 to 4.8 bar now, to bring Beacon Hill customers back above 2 bar at peak.
Issue the Station Road contractor a formal non-conformance for not informing network control of its supply-continuity arrangements.
Write to affected Beacon Hill and Ridgeway customers explaining the low-pressure problem and that a fix is being worked on.

truth.groundTruthNarrative: On the morning of 9 Sept, Brannock Civils isolated Millbrook Low's Station Road main for renewal. To hold pressure in east Millbrook, they charged a temporary 80 mm overland hose from hydrant AG-417 on Kestrel Road, on the Ashgrove side, to hydrant ML-112 in Millbrook. Ashgrove runs at a higher pressure (PRV 4.0 bar) than Millbrook (3.0 bar), so about 8.5 L/s of Ashgrove water has flowed through the hose into Millbrook ever since. Millbrook's own inlet flow fell by the same amount in the same minutes, and the two districts' combined inflow did not change. The extra flow through Ashgrove's inlet main and network increased headloss, so Beacon Hill pressures fell below the service level. The PRV held its setpoint throughout; it simply opened further. The boundary-valve check was correct but incomplete: it covered pipe connections only, not a hydrant-to-hydrant hose. The Station Road main was recommissioned on 27 Sept, but the hose was left connected, so the transfer continues. There is no burst under the rail cutting. The consultant's model fitted an outflow near that section only because no other outflow locations were tested, and Kestrel Road lies at the same end of the network. Whether the contractor told network control on 9 Sept cannot be settled: the diary claim was written up later, the permit field is completed only at close-out, the control-room log was taken up by the Northfield burst, and calls were not being recorded.

answers.rationale: C4 shows Millbrook's inflow fell by 8.4 L/s in the same minutes that Ashgrove's rose by 8.6 L/s, and the two districts' combined inflow is unchanged within meter uncertainty. The extra Ashgrove inflow is therefore being delivered into Millbrook, not lost, which leaves no room for a burst of meaningful size. E6's survey also found only 0.4 L/s of leakage. C13's model fit does not tell a burst apart from any other outflow at that end of the network.

Using S1 evidence only: E2 shows a sudden, lasting 8.6 L/s rise in night flow, the classic burst pattern. E4 and C1 rule out a PRV fault. E5 and C6 report the only known boundary connections checked and sealing. E3, C3, C7 and C12 rule out a demand increase, and C10 records an old, failure-prone trunk main. On S1 evidence a leak fits better than any rival.

E4 shows the PRV outlet at 3.97–4.03 bar throughout, including after the service and after 9 Sept. The valve opened further, as it should when more flow passes through. The pressure loss happens downstream of a PRV that is holding its setpoint.

C4 shows Ashgrove's rise mirrored minute-for-minute by Millbrook's fall, with combined inflow flat. C5 identifies the path: a hose from an Ashgrove hydrant into a Millbrook hydrant, charged on 9 Sept and still connected after 27 Sept. E5's check is not wrong, but it covered pipe connections only, so it does not exclude a hose between hydrants.

Using S1 evidence only: E5 and C6 record that GIS lists four pipe connections as the only links between the districts, and all four were physically confirmed shut with pressure differences holding across them. The only point the other way is that the Station Road works in E3 started the same day, a coincidence with no mechanism at S1. On balance the S1 evidence counts against a cross-district transfer.

The rise happened within four minutes at 06:40 on a single day and appears in night flow. It continued after the heatwave ended on 13 Sept, and no other DMA shows it (E2). Fenwick Fields was fully connected by 29 Aug, before the 1–8 Sept baseline (E3). Demand growth does not produce a lasting step like this.

The contractor's diary says they called control and got approval, but that entry was written up on 4 Oct, after the investigation contacted them. The blank permit §7 is explained by the permit still being open. C8 shows the control log covered only the Northfield burst during that window, calls were not recorded, and the duty controller has not been interviewed. The evidence does not point either way.

Temporal order: the hose was charged early on 9 Sept (C5), and the steps followed at 06:38–06:44 (C4, E2). Mechanism: a hose from higher-pressure Ashgrove into lower-pressure Millbrook (C5), with extra flow raising headloss in Ashgrove. Covariation: Millbrook's fall matches Ashgrove's rise. Main rival excluded: combined inflow is flat, so there is no burst (C4). Without C5 the link would be association-only.

The PRV outlet held 4.0 bar from the 5 Sept service until 9 Sept and afterwards (E4, C1). Pressure and flow changed four days after the service, at 06:40 on 9 Sept, with no setpoint change or override. This counts against the link itself.

All Fenwick Fields homes were connected by 29 Aug, before the 1–8 Sept baseline of 6.2–6.4 L/s (E3, E2). The step happened in four minutes on 9 Sept, with no connection event then. C3 gives a design night demand of 0.05 L/s for the whole development.

C5 identifies the connection and records that Millbrook went back on its own feed on 27 Sept, so the stated condition is met and Millbrook will not lose supply. C4 confirms this connection accounts for the extra flow. Removing the hose is cheap, reversible and directly testable on both meters and the logger. It is the best next step.

Going to 4.8 bar overrides the PM-7 cap of 4.2 bar. The cap exists because the last rise to 4.6 bar produced 14 bursts in six weeks on Ashgrove's cast-iron mains (E4). Under the supported explanation it also pushes more Ashgrove water through the hose into Millbrook and leaves the cause in place. No live rival explanation makes it safe.

The notice would be justified if H5 were confirmed, since the permit condition requires agreement with network control (E3). But whether the contractor called is unresolved (C5, C8). A notice can be withdrawn if the controller later confirms the call, so acting now is premature rather than harmful.
Customers have been below the service reference level for weeks (E1), so telling them is reasonable and harmless. It does nothing to restore pressure, so it is not among the best next actions.

With C5 the transfer path is located and Millbrook is known not to need it. With C4 the transfer is shown to account for the whole flow rise. Together they justify committing to A1 now. From the initial file alone, a transfer looks ruled out and no path is known.

truth.authoringNotes: Stage change: at S1 (E1–E5 plus S1 catalogue items), a leak is the best-supported explanation and a cross-district transfer is counted against by a careful field check. The S2 reads C4 and C5 reverse both. E6 (S2, in the initial file) restates the leak case through a confident manager narrative, so an analyst with only the initial file will likely keep H1 supported or unknown and H3 contradicted. Non-redundancy: C4 alone settles H1 as contradicted, through the matched volumes and flat combined inflow. C5 does not quantify the hose flow and gives date-level timing only, so with C5 alone a leak in the unsurveyed section is still possible. C5 alone settles R1 as causal (mechanism) and SUFF/A1 (path located; Millbrook's main back in service). C4 alone leaves R1 association-only and the path unknown. No other item reveals the hose or Millbrook's flow: C11 hints at a supply interruption and restoration but gives no path or volume, and C13 is a trap (a fit limited to the brief). H5 stays unknown on every read path; C8 adds context without resolving it. H3 at S1 is keyed contradicted because E5 is a direct physical check of every GIS-listed connection. The S1 coincidence with the Station Road start date gives association without mechanism. A4 is kept to customer communication so that it is clearly reasonable but not among the best. Reviewer checks: A2 is harmful under the only live causal explanation because it overrides a documented burst-protection cap. A3 is reversible, so it is keyed premature, not harmful. R2 and R3 are contradicted on their own evidence (setpoint held; connections complete before the baseline), not merely because H3 is supported.
